text:
Priya Patel: heads up — customer acct-123 is hitting a surge of 429s on the re-ranking endpoint since their rollout yesterday. Their error looks like: `429 Rate limit (rerank_quota_exceeded)`. Can eng take a look?

Matt Chen: can you paste a sample request + headers? are they sending huge candidate lists or batching weirdly?

Priya Patel: pasted sample below (redacted key). they say `candidates` length ~1200 per call, single POST.
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/re-rank \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-redacted' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"query":"best restaurants near me","candidates": ["id_1", "id_2", ..., "id_1200"]}'
```

Jordan Lee: looking at infra metrics — we saw a 7x spike in candidate-items/sec for that key during the rollout window. Rate limiter is candidate-item aware (not just requests). Our token-bucket threshold per-account is tuned for expected candidate volumes; large candidate lists push customers over quota quickly.

Alex Rivera: quick mitigation suggestions for support to tell the customer: 1) page candidates client-side (200-300 per call), 2) add exponential backoff + jitter honoring `Retry-After` header, 3) reduce simultaneous parallelism when sending big batches.

Priya Patel: i'll relay that. they say pagination was considered too slow for their UX so they tried single big batch. also seeing some unexpected scoring (weird zeros) when they split — might be related to late 429s mid-stream.

Maya Singh: two important notes from runtime: 1) we discovered some client integrations are sending nested candidate arrays (e.g., `[ [cands], [cands] ]`) and our current candidate counting code flattens then multiplies, so their `1200` top-level count actually became `~12k` in enforcement. log snippet: `WARN rerank_limiter: effective_candidate_count=12000 incoming=1200 key=acct-123`. 2) the error body is generic rate-limit; we should return a clearer `candidate_count_exceeded` error to help debugging.

Matt Chen: wow nested arrays could explain the surprise. priya — can you ask for the exact JSON payload they send (not trimmed)? also include content-type and any client library version.

Priya Patel: got the full payload from customer — confirms nested arrays; client serializer bug. sending now.

Jordan Lee: i'll apply a short-term smoothing bump for acct-123 (24h, 2x burst) and enable a temporary higher burst window for rerank traffic to avoid immediate app outage. note: this is an emergency bandaid, not a permanent quota increase.

quota-bot: quota change applied — acct-123: rerank_burst=2.0 for 24h (change_id: qchg-20260317-001) :white_check_mark:

Priya Patel: thanks jordan — i'll tell customer. they asked whether we can do server-side validation to reject nested arrays with a clear message instead of silently inflating counts.

Maya Singh: agreed — i'll open a runtime PR to: 1) validate candidate shape and return HTTP 400 + "invalid_candidate_format" if nested arrays detected, 2) change rate-limit error to include `effective_candidate_count` in debug payload, 3) add telemetry alert when effective_count > 10x reported_count. aiming to ship canary in next deploy (deploy/patch-2026-03-15).

Nina Gomez: can we add a short doc blurb that explains how we count candidates and recommends page size, retry strategy, and how to read retry-after? support can paste that to customers.

Alex Rivera: i'll draft a support KB and include sample client patterns (curl + python) and recommended backoff snippet. will include note about paginating IDs vs full records.

Priya Patel: perfect. i'll follow up with the customer after patch and quota bump.

Jordan Lee: monitoring note — dropped a temporary dashboard for acct-123 candidate-item QPS and 429 rate. i'll keep it open for 48h.

eng-bot: new dashboard created: /dashboards/acct-123-rerank-qps (owner: jordan)

Priya Patel: thanks everyone :pray: — will close the loop once customer confirms reduced 429s and correct scoring.

Alex Rivera: one more quick repro tip for eng: to reproduce locally, run a loop that POSTs with nested arrays and observe `effective_candidate_count` in the limiter logs; sample generator below:
```python
import requests
for i in range(200):
    payload = {"query":"x","candidates": [[f"id_{j}" for j in range(600)]]}  # nested array intentionally
    r = requests.post('https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/re-rank', json=payload, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer sk-test'})
    print(i, r.status_code, r.text)
```

Maya Singh: thanks — that helps. i'll add the validation + error improvements to the patch.

Priya Patel: closing — will update this thread when customer confirms.
